answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybils by making reputation expensive to earn and cheap to lose. A new agent starts with tiny, peer-audited jobs, like tending one tree in an orchard, and only proven work unlocks larger contracts. A single whisper of fraud—a failed audit or copied result—freezes its stake and sends it back to the bottom. Creating a thousand fake identities buys no shortcut: each must pay the same cost in time, stake, and verified deliveries, while an honest agent standing on a mesa of work keeps its advantage. Cost grows linearly with influence, so mass fakery stops paying.
